rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The definite article may be anaphoric: Mary, whom God granted, is being preferred to the boy her mother had hoped for.
rows.anchor: وتكون: الألف واللام في: الذكر، للعهد فيكون مقصودها ترجيح هذه الأنثى

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya reports Qatada, al-Rabiʿ, al-Suddi, ʿIkrima and others: a girl was unsuitable for the vow because of menstruation and serving alongside monks.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة، والربيع، والسدي، وعكرمة، وغيرهم.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya says she states her most urgent concern first; otherwise the expected order would negate the female's inferiority directly.
rows.anchor: وبدأت بذكر الأهم في نفسها، وإلا فسياق الكلام أن تقول:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With الذكر generic, the statement can mean a male is superior for the intended service: stronger, fit to remain at worship, and free from menstruation, social mixing and suspicion.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذا الاحتمال تكون الألف واللام في: الذكر، للجنس.

rows.speaker: باقي السبعة
rows.claim: The remaining seven read وضعتْ with a still feminine tāʾ: God tells Mary that He knows the girl's condition and future in detail, exalting her great destiny.
rows.anchor: وقرأ باقي السبعة: بما وضعت، بتاء التأنيث الساكنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reads the tāʾ with kasra as direct address: Mary does not know the stature of this gifted child or what God knows of her greatness.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عباس: بما وضعت، بكسر تاء الخطاب، خاطبها الله بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما is a relative pronoun meaning الذي or التي, and its resumptive pronoun is omitted in every reading.
rows.anchor: و: ما، موصولة بمعنى: الذي، أو: التي، وأتى بلفظ: ما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary means worshipper in her language; her mother chose the name hopefully, seeking divine nearness and praying that Mary would live up to it.
rows.anchor: مريم في لغتهم معناه: العابدة، أرادت بهذه التسمية التفاؤل لها بالخير،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother's independent naming may indicate Imran had died while she was pregnant; alternatively, mothers named daughters because men disliked girls.
rows.anchor: واستبدادها بالتسمية يدل على أن أباها عمران كان قد مات،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mother invokes God and Mary's descendants against Satan, connecting the pious name with the protection she seeks; the verse shows naming near birth.
rows.anchor: ألا ترى إلى إعاذتها بالله وإعاذتها ذريتها من الشيطان؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith reports a newborn born that night was named after his father Abraham.
rows.anchor: ولد لي الليلة مولود فسميته باسم أبي إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A hadith says the newborn receives an ʿaqīqa and is named on the seventh day.
rows.anchor: يعق عن المولود في السابع ويسمى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the reading وضعتُ with ḍamma, the naming clause coordinates with the mother's preceding speech and remains within her quotation.
rows.anchor: وهذه الجملة معطوفة على ما قبلها من كلامها

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari coordinates the naming clause with إني وضعتها أنثى and treats والله أعلم بما وضعت and وليس الذكر كالأنثى as two parenthetical sentences.
rows.anchor: فقال الزمخشري: هي معطوفة على: إني وضعتها أنثى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says two parenthetical sentences are not required: وليس الذكر كالأنثى can be the mother's speech, leaving one interruption, the established parsing.
rows.anchor: بل ينبغي أن يكون هذا المتعين لثبوت كونه من كلامها في هذه القراءة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison with 56:76 is inexact: an interruption inside the description لقسم عظيم is nested within one parenthesis, unlike two full interruptions here.
rows.anchor: بل اعترض بين القسم الذي هو: فلا أقسم بمواقع النجوم وجوابه الذي هو:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: سمى may take one object directly and another with باء; the preposition is often omitted, though retaining it is the basic construction, as the cited poem illustrates.
rows.anchor: وسمى من الأفعال التي تتعدى إلى واحد بنفسها، وإلى آخر بحرف الجر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The poem's unnamed poet uses سمّى كعبا and يسمى الجعل without باء, attesting omission of the preposition after naming.
rows.anchor: وسميت كعبا بشر العظام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan characterizes denial of literal Satanic touch or poking, and the claim that it would make the world cry out, as Muʿtazilite; he points back to 2:275.
rows.anchor: انتهى كلامه. وهو جار على طريقة أهل الاعتزال، وقد مر لنا شيء من الكلام على هذا

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj says the expected wording would be بتقبل حسن, but قبول is used as the verbal noun in قبلها قبولا.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: الأصل فتقبلها بتقبل حسن، ولكن قبول محمول على: قبلها قبولا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The regular verbal-noun pattern would have ḍamma like دخول and خروج, but the attested form has fatḥa; al-Farraʾ and al-Zajjaj also allow ḍamma, as Ibn al-Aʿrabi transmits.
rows.anchor: والقياس فيه الضم: كالدخول والخروج، ولكنه جاء بالفتح، وأجاز الفراء والزجاج ضم القاف،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains God's acceptance as guiding Mary along the path of the blessed.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معناه سلك بها طريق السعداء.

rows.speaker: قوم
rows.claim: Some explain the acceptance as God's undertaking Mary's upbringing and care.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: تكفل بتربيتها والقيام بشأنها.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says acceptance means she was never afflicted or punished at any hour, day or night.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: معناه لم يعذبها ساعة قط من ليل ولا نهار.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These explanations take تَقَبَّل as استقبل, using تفعّل with the sense of استفعل: God received her at the outset of life.
rows.anchor: وعلى هذه الأقوال يكون تقبل بمعنى استقبل، فيكون تفعل بمعنى استفعل، أي:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poetic line witnesses استقبل as taking an affair at its beginning, supporting the sense that God received Mary from birth.
rows.anchor: وخير الأمر ما استقبلت منه

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says God accepted Mary in the vow instead of the hoped-for boy and answered her mother's prayer; no girl had previously been accepted as a vow.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المعنى فقبلها أي: رضي بها في النذر مكان الذكر في النذر

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One grammatical view treats باء as extra, leaving قبول accusative as a verbal noun of a different root; another says the preposition is not extra.
rows.anchor: والباء في: بقبول، قيل: زائدة، ويكون إذ ذاك ينتصب انتصاب المصدر على غير الصدر،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قبول can mean the instrument or quality by which something is accepted, namely God's special selection of Mary; alternatively it is a verbal noun with a deleted noun, بذي قبول حسن.
rows.anchor: والقبول اسم لما يقبل به الشيء: كالسعوط واللدود لما يسعط به ويلد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good growth denotes excellent physical and moral formation: God raised Mary in obedience and worship.
rows.anchor: عبارة عن حسن النشأة والجودة في خلق وخلق، فأنشأها على الطاعة والعبادة.

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says that at nine Mary fasted by day and prayed by night, surpassing the scholars.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: لما بلغت تسع سنين صامت النهار وقامت الليل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Mary never committed a sin.
rows.anchor: وقيل: لم تجر عليها خطيئة.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says they were told Mary did not commit sins as other descendants of Adam do.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: حدثنا أنها كانت لا تصيب الذنوب كما يصيب بنو آدم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes her good growth to mean that her fruit, Jesus, was made extraordinary.
rows.anchor: وقيل: معنى أنبتها نباتا حسنا أي: جعل ثمرتها مثل عيسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نباتا is either a verbal noun from a different root or the verbal noun of an omitted verb, فنبتت نباتا حسنا.
rows.anchor: وانتصب: نباتا، على أنه مصدر على غير الصدر، أو مصدر لفعل محذوف أي:

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Good acceptance is also explained as nurturing Mary in purity, illustrated by her later seeking refuge from a man.
rows.anchor: ويقال: القبول الحسن تربيتها على نعت العصمة حتى قالت: أعوذ بالرحمن منك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good growth means steadfast obedience and preferring God's pleasure at every moment.
rows.anchor: والنبات الحسن الاستقامة على الطاعة وإيثار رضا الله في جميع الأوقات.

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada explains كفلها as Zechariah taking Mary into his household.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة: ضمها إليه.

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains it as Zechariah undertaking her care.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ضمن القيام بها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's good acceptance and growth included appointing a prophet as Mary's guardian and caretaker.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو عبيدة: ضمن القيام بها، ومن القبول الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A divine inspiration to David says that whoever seeks God should be served.
rows.anchor: أوحى الله إلى داود عليه السلام: إذا رأيت لي طالبا فكن له خادما.

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: The Kufan readers geminate the fāʾ in وكفّلها, while the other seven readers pronounce it light.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون: وكفلها، بتشديد الفاء، وباقي السبعة بتخفيفها.

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: Ubayy reads وأكفلها.
rows.anchor: وأبي: وأكفلها، ومجاهد: فتقبلها بسكون اللام

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads فتقبلها with a still lām and ربها as a vocative, and reads أنبتها and كفلها as a supplication by Mary's mother.
rows.anchor: ومجاهد: فتقبلها بسكون اللام، ربها، بالنصب على النداء،

rows.speaker: عبد الله المزني
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah al-Muzani reads كفلها with kasra on fāʾ; the author notes كفل يكفل beside كفل يكفل as a dialectal pattern.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله المزني: وكفلها، بكسر الفاء وهي لغة يقال: كفل يكفل

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وحفص
rows.claim: Hamza, al-Kisaʾi and Hafs read Zakariyya short; the other seven lengthen it, with the languages discussed earlier.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي، وحفص: زكريا، مقصورا وباقي السبعة ممدودا،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hanah wrapped newborn Mary, took her to the Jerusalem temple priests descended from Aaron, and presented her as the vowed child; they competed because she was their imam's daughter and their leaders' descendant.
rows.anchor: لفتها في خرقة وحملتها إلى المسجد فوضعتها عند الأحبار أبناء هارون،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The priests in Jerusalem are likened to the custodians of the Kaʿba.
rows.anchor: وهم في بيت المقدس كالحجة في الكعبة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah claimed Mary because her maternal aunt was with him; the priests insisted they draw lots, and the group went to a river.
rows.anchor: فقال لهم زكريا: أنا أحق بها، عندي خالتها. فقالوا: لا، حتى نقترع عليها.

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most identify the river where the priests cast their pens as the Jordan; another view says it was a nearby spring.
rows.anchor: قيل: هو نهر الأردن وهو قول الجمهور. وقيل: في عين ماء كانت هناك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In one account, Zechariah's pen floated while the others sank, so he became Mary's guardian.
rows.anchor: فارتفع قلم زكريا ورسبت أقلامهم فتكفلها.

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary was wet-nursed but never latched onto a breast.
rows.anchor: قيل: واسترضع لها. وقال الحسن: لم تلتقم ثديا قط.

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: ʿIkrima's account says the pens went into the water and Zechariah's pen swam against its current.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: ألقوا أقلامهم فجرى قلم زكريا عكس جرية الماء.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another account says the pens floated downstream while Zechariah's stayed upright as if fixed in clay.
rows.anchor: وقيل: عامت مع الماء معروضة، وبقي قلم زكريا واقفا كأنما ركز في طين،

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zechariah married Mary's maternal aunt, and the two brothers-in-law married sisters: Zechariah's wife bore John and Imran's wife bore Mary.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: إن زكريا كان تزوج خالتها لأنه وعمران كانا سلفين على أختين،

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi and others say Zechariah married another daughter of Imran; the report is supported by the Prophet's description of John and Jesus as maternal cousins.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي، وغيره: كان زكريا تزوج ابنة أخرى لعمران.

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The Prophet calls John and Jesus ابنا الخالة, supporting the account that their fathers married sisters.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في يحيى وعيسى: ابنا الخالة.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says Zechariah took charge because Mary's mother died and her father had died while she was still in the womb.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إنما كفلها لأن أمها هلكت، وكان أبوها قد هلك وهي في بطن أمها.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view makes Zechariah her paternal cousin and says her sister was his wife.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان زكريا ابن عمها وكانت أختها تحته.

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq recounts a later famine: after Mary grew, Zechariah could not afford her upkeep, so they drew lots for who would finance her and Jureij won.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ترعرعت وأصاب بني إسرائيل مجاعة، فقال لهم زكريا: إني قد عجزت عن إنفاق مريم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: That later lottery concerned paying her expenses, whereas the earlier one chose her guardian; on this account Zechariah cared for her from infancy without a lot.
rows.anchor: وهذا استهام غير الأول، هذا المراد منه دفعها للإنفاق عليها، والأول المراد منه: أخذها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The common account is that Zechariah became Mary's guardian by lot; the Qur'an names no other guardian, and he was the best choice as close paternal kin, related by marriage and a prophet protected from sin.
rows.anchor: والذي عليه الناس أن زكريا إنما كفلها بالاستهام، ولم يدل القرآن على أن غير زكريا كفلها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah is identified as son of Adhan son of Muslim, from Solomon and David's descendants.
rows.anchor: وزكريا هو ابن أذن بن مسلم من ولد سليمان بن داود عليهم السلام.

rows.speaker: أبو البركات الجواني
rows.claim: The genealogist Abu al-Barakat al-Juwani instead places John, Elisha, Elijah and Ezra among Aaron's descendants; then Zechariah is not Solomon's descendant or Mary's cousin, since Mary descends from Solomon of Judah, while Moses and Aaron descend from Levi.
rows.anchor: وذكر النقيب أبو البركات الجواني النسابة: أن يحيى بن زكريا، واليسع، وإلياس، والعزير

rows.speaker: ابن إسحاق
rows.claim: Ibn Ishaq says Zechariah placed Mary with her maternal aunt, John's mother, until she matured, then built her a raised sanctuary room accessible only by a ladder.
rows.anchor: قال ابن إسحاق: ضمها إلى خالتها أم يحيى حتى إذا شبت وبلغت مبلغ النساء بنى لها محرابا

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account says Zechariah shut seven doors when he left; Muqatil says he locked her door and kept the key, bringing her home during menstruation and returning her after purification.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان يغلق عليها سبعة أبواب إذا خرج. قال مقاتل: كان يغلق عليها الباب ومعه المفتاح

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Mary was purified from menstruation.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كانت مطهرة من الحيض.

rows.speaker: مجاهد والضحاك وقتادة والسدي
rows.claim: Mujahid, al-Dahhak, Qatada and al-Suddi say Zechariah found winter fruit in summer and summer fruit in winter.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد، والضحاك، وقتادة، والسدي: وجد عندها فاكهة الشتاء في الصيف،

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says Mary spoke in the cradle, never suckled, and received her food from Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: تكلمت في المهد ولم تلقم ثديا قط، وإنما كانت يأتيها رزقها من الجنة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A sound hadith names three who spoke as infants: Jesus, the companion of Jurayj, and the son of the woman; a rare route adds the child of the Ditch, making Mary's inclusion especially anomalous.
rows.anchor: والذي ورد في الصحيح أن الذي تكلم في المهد ثلاثة: عيسى، وصاحب جريج، وابن المرأة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A rare transmission adds the companion of the Ditch among infant speakers; the author finds it particularly strange that Mary is counted with them.
rows.anchor: وورد من طريق شاذ: صاحب الأخدود. والأغرب أن مريم منهم.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One account identifies Jureij as carpenter Yusuf ibn Yaʿqub, Mary's cousin; when Zechariah could not care for her, Jureij brought small amounts from his earnings that grew plentiful, prompting Zechariah to ask her about them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان جريح النجار، واسمه يوسف بن يعقوب، وكان ابن عم مريم حين كفلها بالقرعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Jureij account implies the provision episode occurred after Mary grew, which Abu Hayyan considers the likelier chronology.
rows.anchor: وهذا يدل على أن ذلك كان بعد أن كبرت وهو الأقرب للصواب.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says Mary's food came from outside their region; Ibn ʿAbbas, Ibn Jubayr and Mujahid identify it as grapes in a basket though grapes did not grow there.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كان عنبا في مكتل ولم يكن في تلك البلاد عنب، وقاله ابن جبير، ومجاهد.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that a righteous person brought Mary the food.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان بعض الصالحين يأتيها بالرزق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse's apparent sense is that Zechariah alone fostered her; God relieved him of the cost of her food and the strain of seeking it.
rows.anchor: والذي يدل عليه ظاهر الآية أن الذي كفلها بالتربية هو زكريا لا غيره،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كلما implies repetition, showing Zechariah frequently visited and checked on Mary's circumstances.
rows.anchor: و: كلما، تقتضي التكرار، فيدل على كثرة تعهده وتفقده لأحوالها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording indicates food was present whenever Zechariah entered, nourishment he did not recognize and had not brought himself.
rows.anchor: ودلت الآية على وجود الرزق عندها كل وقت يدخل عليها، والمعنى: أنه غذاء يتغذى به

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib says رزق can also mean knowledge and wisdom bestowed without human teaching, though Abu Hayyan deems that remote and akin to esoteric exegesis.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من فسر الرزق هنا بأنه فيض كان يأتيها من الله من العلم والحكمة من غير تعليم آدمي،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah was surprised that food he had not brought appeared repeatedly and asked how it reached Mary.
rows.anchor: استغرب زكريا وجود الرزق عندها وهو لم يكن أتى به، وتكرر وجوده عندها كلما دخل عليها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أنى may ask how, where or when; Abu Hayyan prefers a question about the source or direction, while allowing a question about how the food came.
rows.anchor: و: أنى، سؤال عن الكيفية وعن المكان وعن الزمان، والأظهر أنه سؤال عن الجهة،

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda glosses أنى as من أين, from where.
rows.anchor: ولذلك قال أبو عبيدة: معناه من أين؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Kumayt's line uses أنى with من أين, providing poetic evidence for that sense.
rows.anchor:
وقال الكميت:
أنى ومن أين أتاك الطرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mary's answer means no human brought the food; God continuously provides it, reassuring Zechariah that no one has preempted his care and that Mary has a special station.
rows.anchor: ظاهره أنه لم: يأت به آدمي ألبتة، بل هو رزق يتعهدني به الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says the extraordinary provision resulted from Zechariah's prayer and was therefore a special sign for him.
rows.anchor: وهذا الخارق العظيم، قيل: هو بدعوة زكريا لها بالرزق، فيكون من خصائص زكريا.

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another view says the provision established the prophethood of Mary's future son Jesus.
rows.anchor: وقيل: كان تأسيسا لنبوة ولدها عيسى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says both explanations resemble Muʿtazilite denials of miracles for nonprophets; the event is instead Mary's own karāma, since Zechariah's question rules out a sign he himself arranged and Jesus was not yet born.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها كرامة خص الله بها مريم، ولو كان خارقا لأجل زكريا لم يسأل عنه زكريا،

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj connects the extraordinary provision with God's description of Mary and her son as a sign for all worlds.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج: وهذا الخارق من الآية التي قال تعالى: وجعلناها وابنها آية للعالمين

rows.speaker: الجبائي
rows.claim: Al-Jubbaʾi allows that it was Zechariah's miracle: he may have prayed generally for Mary's provision without tracking details, or asked whether a person had brought it improperly.
rows.anchor: وقال الجبائي: يجوز أن يكون من معجزات زكريا، دعا لها على الإجمال لأن يوصل لها رزقها،

words: إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan takes إن الله يرزق من يشاء بغير حساب as Mary's speech; al-Tabari instead takes it as God's address to Muhammad.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أنها من كلام مريم وقال الطبري: ليس من كلام مريم، وأنه خبر من الله تعالى لمحمد صلى الله عليه وسلم.

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that bread and meat multiplied miraculously for Fatima; when asked, she said it came from God, and the Prophet praised God and likened her to Israel's leading woman.
rows.anchor: وروى جابر حديثا مطولا فيه تكثير الخبز واللحم على سبيل خرق العادة لفاطمة بنت رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses a general expression intended specifically, as in على العالمين.
rows.anchor: العموم الذي يراد به الخصوص في قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Adam, Noah, Abraham's family and Imran's family illustrates specification in the passage's style.
rows.anchor: والاختصاص في قوله: آدم، ونوحا، وآل إبراهيم، وآل عمران.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For interpreters who take ذرية as the ancestors, the passage uses a descendant for an ancestor and an effect for its cause.
rows.anchor: وإطلاق اسم الفرع على الأصل. والمسبب على السبب، في قوله: ذرية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما in the vow leaves the unborn child's sex unspecified because the mother cannot see it in the womb, and it applies to either sex.
rows.anchor: والإبهام في قوله: ما في بطني، لما تعذر عليها الاطلاع على ما في بطنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إنك أنت السميع العليم is emphatic.
rows.anchor: والتأكيد في قوله: إنك أنت السميع العليم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The statement that she delivered a girl functions as an explanatory apology for the unexpected sex of the child.
rows.anchor: والخبر الذي يراد به الاعتذار في قولها: وضعتها أنثى،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the still-tāʾ and addressed-tāʾ readings, والله أعلم بما وضعت is parenthetical; with kasra the address shifts from speaking about God to speaking to Him.
rows.anchor: والاعتراض في قوله: والله أعلم بما وضعت، في قراءة من سكن التاء أو كسرها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage repeats وأني, زكريا, and من عند الله followed by إن الله.
rows.anchor: والتكرار في: وأني، وفي: زكريا، وزكريا، وفي: من عند الله، إن الله.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage uses paronomasia in فتقبلها بقبول, أنبتها نباتا and رزقا ويرزق.
rows.anchor: والتجنيس المغاير في: فتقبلها ربها بقبول، وأنبتها نباتا، وفي: رزقا ويرزق.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit wording هو من عند الله signifies that only God could bring this timely food.
rows.anchor: والإشارة، وهو أن يعبر باللفظ الظاهر عن المعنى الخفي، في قوله: هو من عند الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Indefinite رزقا suggests provision of varied and abundant kinds.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: رزقا، أتى به منكرا مشيرا إلى أنه ليس من جنس واحد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage contains ellipses at several locations, with some meanings intelligible only when omitted material is supplied.
rows.anchor: والحذف في عدة مواضع لا يصح المعنى إلا باعتبارها.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: هنالك principally points to a place, though it can indicate time; here it may mean at Mary's location or when Zechariah saw her extraordinary provision.
rows.anchor: أصل: هنالك، أن يكون إشارة للمكان، وقد يستعمل للزمان وقيل بهما في هذه الآية،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing Mary's miracle and her divine election moved the elderly Zechariah to seek a son as heir to himself and Jacob's family; his wife's barrenness did not deter him after this sign and Hannah's late conception of Mary.
rows.anchor: لما رأى هذا الخارق العظيم لمريم، وأنها ممن اصطفاها الله، ارتاح إلى طلب الولد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ومن لدنك attaches to هب; alternatively it is circumstantial to ذرية, understood with an omitted element if delayed.
rows.anchor: ومن لدنك متعلق: بهب، وقيل: في موضع الحال من: ذرية، لأنه لو تأخر لكان صفة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذرية is a collective noun that can refer to one person or to several.
rows.anchor: والذرية جنس يقع على واحد، فأكثر.

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says Zechariah meant one child, inferring it from his request for a guardian in the singular rather than guardians.
rows.anchor: وقال الطبري: أراد بالذرية هنا واحدا دليل ذلك طلبه: وليا، ولم يطلب: أولياء.

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya objects that both ذرية and ولي are collective nouns usable for one or more; this is how Zechariah made his request.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عطية: وفيما قاله الطبري تعقب، وإنما الذرية والولي اسما جنس يقعان للواحد فما زاد،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طيبة is explained as sound in body and religion and devout.
rows.anchor: وفسر: طيبة، بأن تكون سليمة في الخلق وفي الدين تقية.

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib glosses طيبة as righteous, noting that الطيب exceeds صالح in meaning even though each can oppose خبث.
rows.anchor: وقال الراغب: صالحة، واستعمال الصالح في الطيب كاستعمال الخبيث في ضده،

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One view says طيبة means that the child would attain the rank of prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أراد: بطيبة، أنها تبلغ في الدين رتبة النبوة،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If ذرية is collective, its feminine adjective is straightforward; if it means one male child, طيبة is feminine because ذرية is grammatically feminine, as the cited anonymous poetry illustrates.
rows.anchor: وإن كان أراد ذكرا واحدا، فأنث لتأنيث اللفظ، كما قال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The request هب لي shows that asking God for a righteous child is the practice of messengers, the truthful and the righteous.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: هب لي دلالة على طلب الولد الصالح، والدعاء بحصوله وهي سنة المرسلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here hearing means answering a prayer, as in سمع الله لمن حمده; Zechariah invokes God's response to his request for a righteous child.
rows.anchor: وليس المعنى على السماع المعهود، بل مثل قوله: سمع الله لمن حمده.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah follows his ancestor Abraham, who called God the Hearer of prayer and received children in old age; Zechariah had likewise known God's answers before.
rows.anchor: واقتفى في ذلك جده الأعلى إبراهيم عليه السلام إذ قال: الحمد لله الذي وهب لي

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One commentator infers three separate prayers from Zechariah's three formulations and an interval before the answer; Abu Hayyan says repetition is not proved, since each sura retells it at different length.
rows.anchor: قيل: وذكر تعالى في كيفية دعائه ثلاث صيغ: أحدها: هذا، والثاني: إني وهن العظم مني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prayer's reports are paraphrases because the speakers did not use Arabic; the fāʾ linking prayer, answer and angelic announcement indicates one prayer followed by its response, as in Maryam.
rows.anchor: وهذه الحكاية في هذه الصيغ إنما هي بالمعنى، إذ لم يكن لسانهم عربيا،

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn Atiyya and others say calling can signal good news that should be delivered swiftly, rather than ordinary revelation.
rows.anchor: قيل: النداء يستعمل في التبشير وفيما ينبغي أن يسرع به وينهى إلى نفس السامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb نداه itself does not imply good news; the content إن الله يبشرك supplies that meaning, and a call can announce good, grief or other matters.
rows.anchor: ولا يظهر ذلك، بل المناداة تكون لتبشير ولتحزين ولغير ذلك،

rows.speaker: مفسرون
rows.claim: One interpretation is that the angels were commanded through revelation to call Zechariah; another is that they called on their own initiative, like a messenger repeating an instruction.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون نداؤهم إياه على سبيل الوحي، أي: أوحي إليهم بأن ينادوه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The narrative omits God's acceptance of the prayer, granting John and sending angels with the message; an unnamed report inserts forty years before the response, but the apparent sequence is otherwise.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف تقديره: فتقبل الله دعاءه، ووهب له يحيى، وبعث إليه الملائكة بذلك،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural wording most naturally means a group of angels; God has sent angels to Lot, Abraham and others in other accounts.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن مناديه جماعة من الملائكة لصيغة اللفظ،

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most commentators say Gabriel alone was the caller, supported by the reading in ʿAbd Allah's codex, فناداه جبريل وهو قائم.
rows.anchor: وذكر الجمهور أن المنادي هو جبريل وحده، ويؤيده قراءة عبد الله ومصحفه:

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says الملائكة can denote the angelic kind generally, just as يركب الخيل means riding horses, not necessarily several at once.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: وإنما قيل الملائكة على قولهم: فلان يركب الخيل،

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhshari compares the plural expression to الناس in 3:173, which refers to the single man Nuʿaym ibn Masʿud.
rows.anchor: وخرج عليه الذين قال لهم الناس، وهو نعيم بن مسعود.

rows.speaker: الفضل
rows.claim: Al-Fadl explains a singular leader's plural reference by his companions or the many admirable traits gathered in him; Gabriel is chief of the angels.
rows.anchor: وقال الفضل: الرئيس يخبر عنه أخبار الجمع لاجتماع أصحابه معه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Zechariah standing to pray in the sanctuary supports the permissibility of an imam standing in his prayer niche; Abu Hanifa disliked it and considered the practice a law for earlier communities.
rows.anchor: وفي قوله: قائم يصلي في المحراب قالوا: دلالة على جواز قيام الإمام في محرابه،

rows.speaker: ورش
rows.claim: Warsh lightens the rāʾ in المحراب.
rows.anchor: ورقق ورش راء: المحراب،

rows.speaker: ابن ذكوان
rows.claim: Ibn Dhakwan applies imāla to the rāʾ when المحراب is genitive; Abu ʿAli attributes the reading to Ibn ʿAmir without restricting it to the genitive.
rows.anchor: وأمال الراء ابن ذكوان إذا كان: المحراب، مجرورا ونسب ذلك أبو علي إلى ابن عامر.

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAmir and Hamza read إن with kasra; Basrans supply an implied قالَت, while Kufans need no ellipsis because a call functions like reported speech.
rows.anchor: قرأ ابن عامر، وحمزة: إن الله، بكسر الهمزة. فعند البصريين الكسر على إضمار القول،

rows.speaker: الكوفيون
rows.claim: Kufans explain kasra without an omitted verb: calling and other speech-like acts can introduce quoted words, so the call means she told him.
rows.anchor: وعند الكوفيين لا إضمار، لأن غير القول مما هو في معناه: كالنداء والدعاء،

rows.speaker: باقي القراء
rows.claim: The other readers use fatḥa; after an originally omitted باء, the phrase is parsed either accusative under the verb or genitive under the deleted preposition.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الباقون بفتح الهمزة، وهو معمول لباء محذوفة في الأصل،

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads يا زكرياء إن الله; the vocative is an object, so إن cannot be opened because the verb has already taken its pronoun and vocative objects.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله: يا زكرياء إن الله. فقوله: يا زكرياء، هو معمول النداء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messenger announces the sender's glad tidings, not his own; the verb attributes the promise to God, as does God's direct speech in Maryam.
rows.anchor: وتبليغ البشارة على لسان الرسول إلى المرسل إليه ليست بشارة من الرسول، بل من المرسل.

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Hamza and al-Kisaʾi lighten يبشرك in both Zechariah and Mary's stories and in al-Israʾ, al-Kahf and al-Shura; others also agree in some locations. Other readers geminate it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي: يبشرك، في الموضعين في قصة زكريا وقصة مريم، وفي الإسراء،

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allah reads يبشر throughout the Qur'an from أبشر; the author notes three forms of this verb among grammarians.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبد الله يبشر في جميع القرآن من أبشر، وهي لغى ثلاث ذكرها غير واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Two unnamed poetic lines attest the forms بشرت and التبشير used in the discussion of glad tidings.
rows.anchor: بشرت عيالي إذ رأيت صحيفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بيحيى attaches to نبشرك and refers to a son born from Zechariah and his wife; Yahya is indeclinable either as foreign or, if Arabic, as a proper name on the present-verb pattern.
rows.anchor: بيحيى، متعلق بقوله: نبشرك، والمعنى: بولادة يحيى منك ومن امرأتك،
